title: The owner's nebulae in the sky: his Veil Nebula and Stellar Bloom pages rendered once and hung as world-fixed planes like the hole, the veil opposite the hole on the horizon, the bloom a quarter turn round and high; the baked galaxies a tenth the size
context: Owner, 2026-10-07: 'the same method we used to represent the blackhole, we will use that to add the veil nebula (twirling-lights-veil.html) on the exact opposite side as the blackhole accretion, on the horizon, small, visible from the base. and (twirling-lights-bloom.html) this stellar bloom elsewhere in the sky. remove the existing galaxies we had, or if trivially cheap to display, keep them but much smaller, further away.' The two pages share one volume ray march (64 steps through a sphere of gas, 4-octave 3D noise, tone-mapped) and differ in their density function and palette; each was saved with its own settings and camera.
outcome: src/fx/nebulae.js carries both scenes verbatim with each page's saved settings (Jade ribbons and Blue iris, detail, density, morph, exposure, zoom, camera, moment), the pages' own stars left out, the picture faded in a circle inside its square with an alpha for the clear sky, rendered once into a 512-pixel still. src/fx/accretion.js now owns the shared pieces: renderShaderStill (the one-shot WebGL context renderAccretion used), stillTexture, skyGlowPlane (the additive plane accretionSkyPlanes builds on, userData.sky saying where it hangs) and turnSkyDirection (a turn round the zenith from the hole's compass point at an elevation). galaxyseed.js SKY_VEIL (turn pi, elevation 0.1, 12 units across 46 out: about 15 degrees) and SKY_BLOOM (turn pi/2, elevation 0.4, 16 across 45 out: about 20 degrees); programme-host.js hangs all three through one helper at creation (the heart at the pole until the world says where) and re-aims the nebulae with the hole once the base stands, so the veil is always the exact opposite side of the sky from the hole as the hull sees it from the bays. The baked galaxies kept (they cost nothing to draw: baked once into the sky cube) at SKY_PRESET.scale 0.1, the bake's floor, two and a half times further and smaller than before; the lab's galaxy-size knob floor lowered to match. --sky-hole now also looks at the veil and the bloom from the hull (SKY-VEIL / SKY-BLOOM notes, the veil asserted opposite the hole): the harness found that showcase.look never turned the camera on its own (the camera chases the travel direction at a bounded rate, and the bay's roll-out owns the camera and rewrites the heading every frame until it hands over; the hole look only worked because the berth faces the Stålheart), so look now sets the travel direction too, hooks.deploying() says when the roll-out is done, and the nebula looks wait for it.
alternatives: Removing the galaxies outright: not needed, the bake costs nothing per frame and the owner allowed keeping them small and far
Rendering the nebulae live each frame: 64 steps of 3D noise a pixel under the game, not for a phone
A fixed world direction for each nebula: the hole is re-aimed per world from the bays toward the Stålheart, so 'the exact opposite side' has to follow it
evidence: scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --sky-hole: SKY HOLE dir [-0.01,0.02,1.00] 40 out 28 across; SKY-VEIL dir [0.01,0.10,-0.99] 46 out 12 across (180 degrees round); SKY-BLOOM dir [0.88,0.47,0.01] 45 out 16 across; stills sky-veil-look (the veil small over the bays' roofs on the opposite horizon) and sky-bloom-look (the blue spiral high over the dish)
npm test (184 programs, test/nebulae.mjs new), npm run check, npm run architecture, npm run build
